question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
The credit for organising/ the successful event was/ given to both Neha and I.
option_2: given to both Neha and I.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. given to both Neha and I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the use of "I" in the phrase "given to both Neha and I".

• Rule: A pronoun that follows a preposition must be in the objective case (me, him, her, us, them), never in the subjective case (I, he, she, we, they). Here, "to" is a preposition, and "Neha and I" is its object.

• Correct form: "given to both Neha and me."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "the successful event was" — this segment is grammatically correct; it fits properly with the passive construction of the sentence.

• Option 3: "The credit for organising" — this is a correct noun phrase acting as the subject of the sentence; no error here.

• Option 4: "No error" — incorrect, since the sentence does contain an error, as explained above.

NOTE

• Common objective-case pronoun errors tested by SSC: "between you and I" (should be "between you and me"), "for him and I" (should be "for him and me").

• Trick to check: remove the other person's name and see if the pronoun still sounds correct — "given to I" sounds wrong, confirming that "me" is required.

question:
Select the word that is similar in meaning (SYNONYM) to the word given below
Malign
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Baleful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Malign" (as an adjective) means evil in nature or effect; harmful, malevolent. (दुष्ट, हानिकारक)
◦ Example: The company's malign influence on the local economy became evident over time.

• The word "Baleful" means threatening harm; menacing or malevolent, which closely matches the meaning of "malign". (अशुभ, हानिकारक)
◦ Example: He gave the intruder a baleful stare.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Nihilistic" (शून्यवादी): rejecting all religious and moral principles, believing that life is meaningless.

• Option 2: "Insurgent" (विद्रोही): a person fighting against an established government or authority; a rebel.

• Option 4: "Radical" (आमूल): relating to fundamental change, or a person who favours extreme political or social reform.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Malign": Malevolent, Malicious, Sinister, Vicious, Pernicious.

• Do not confuse "malign" (evil, harmful) with "benign" (gentle, harmless), which is its antonym.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.
He made me think of an old time magician more than ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. anything.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression "more than anything" (or "more than anything else") is used to emphasise a comparison, meaning to the greatest extent, above all else.

• Rule: In comparative constructions with "more than", the indefinite pronoun "anything" is the standard idiomatic choice when no other specific noun is mentioned for comparison, since it denotes an unlimited, general comparison.

• Applying this to the sentence: "He made me think of an old time magician more than anything." — this means the resemblance to an old-time magician was stronger than any other comparison one could make.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "a thing" is incorrect because it is not idiomatically used after "more than"; it also does not fit as a natural collocation.

• Option 2: "everything" is incorrect because "more than everything" is not standard usage in this comparative sense — "everything" is normally used in affirmative, non-comparative contexts.

• Option 3: "something" is incorrect because it denotes a specific, unspecified single thing, whereas the sentence requires a general, all-encompassing comparison, which "anything" provides.

NOTE

• Indefinite pronouns like "anything", "something", "everything", "nothing" are frequently tested by SSC in fill-in-the-blank questions — remember that "anything" is typically used after comparatives ("more than anything"), negatives, and questions, while "something" is used in affirmative statements.

question:
Choose the option that is the correct direct form of the sentence.
He said that he would be taking a leave of absence for two weeks as there had been a death in his family.
option_1: He said "I am going to take a leave for two weeks as there had been a death in my family".
option_2: He said, "I would be taking a leave of absence for 2 weeks as there been a death in my family
option_3: He said "I will be taking a leave of absence for two week as there is a death in my family".
option_4: He said, "I will be taking a leave of absence for two weeks as there has been a death in my family".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He said, "I will be taking a leave of absence for two weeks as there has been a death in my family".

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is in indirect (reported) speech, using the Future-in-the-Past tense ("would be taking") and the Past Perfect Tense ("had been").

• Rule — converting indirect speech to direct speech:
◦ The reporting verb "said that" is replaced by "said, " " with the reported words placed inside quotation marks.
◦ "would" (future-in-the-past, used for reported future actions) reverts to "will" in direct speech.
◦ "had been" (Past Perfect, used to show an action completed before another past action in reported speech) reverts to "has been" (Present Perfect) in direct speech, since the original speaker's words are being restored to the moment of speaking.
◦ Pronouns and time/place references also revert to what the original speaker actually said: "he" becomes "I", "his family" becomes "my family".

• Applying the rule: "he would be taking" → "I will be taking"; "there had been a death" → "there has been a death"; "for two weeks" remains unchanged as it is a fixed duration, not a specific time reference requiring a shift.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it changes the meaning and structure entirely — "I am going to take a leave" and dropping "of absence" and "has" do not correctly restore the original tense forms.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "would" is wrongly retained in direct speech, and the clause "as there been a death" is grammatically incomplete — it is missing the auxiliary "has".

• Option 3 is incorrect because "two week" should be plural ("two weeks"), and "there is a death" incorrectly uses the Simple Present instead of the required Present Perfect ("there has been a death").

NOTE

• When converting Past Perfect (had + V3) in indirect speech back to direct speech, it usually becomes Present Perfect (has/have + V3), provided the action still holds true relative to the moment of the original speech.

• Modal shifts to remember: will ↔ would, can ↔ could, may ↔ might, shall ↔ should (indirect uses the past/modal form; direct restores the original form).

question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.
P. Fasting also leads to a feeling of rejuvenation and extended life expectancy.
Q. This might be due to the detoxification effect of fasting.
R. A study was performed on earthworms that showed the extension of life thanks to fasting.
S. The experiment was performed in the 1930s by isolating one worm and putting it on a cycle of fasting and feeding.
The isolated worm outlived the other worms by 19 generations, while still maintaining its freshness and youthful physiological characteristics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. PQRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence P introduces the main idea — that fasting leads to rejuvenation and extended life expectancy — and must come first since it sets up the topic of the paragraph.

• Sentence Q logically follows P, as it offers a probable explanation ("This might be due to...") for the claim made in P; the word "This" in Q refers back to the rejuvenating/life-extending effect mentioned in P.

• Sentence R then introduces supporting evidence — a scientific study on earthworms — for the detoxification claim made in Q.

• Sentence S naturally follows R, providing further specific detail about that same study (when it was performed and how), and leads directly into the fixed closing sentence about the isolated worm outliving the others.

• Correct order: P → Q → R → S, i.e. PQRS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (PQSR) is incorrect because it places S (the specific details of the experiment) before R (the general introduction of the study itself), reversing the logical general-to-specific flow.

• Option 2 (PRSQ) is incorrect because it places Q (the explanation "This might be due to...") after S, but "This" in Q must refer back to the claim in P, not to the experimental details in S.

• Option 4 (PSRQ) is incorrect because it places S (experiment details) before R (introduction of the study), and Q last, breaking the cause-and-explanation link with P.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, look for linking words/pronouns ("This", "It", "Also", "However") — they usually refer back to an idea in the immediately preceding sentence and are the key to finding the correct order.

• The sentence that introduces the general topic (without any pronoun reference to prior information) almost always comes first.

question:
Select the option that will improve the (bracketed) part of the sentence. In case of no improvement select the option 'No improvement'.
There's even a (picture by which a witch is riding) a broomstick on the sides of the police cars.
option_2: picture that of a witch riding
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. picture of a witch riding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The original bracketed phrase "picture by which a witch is riding" is grammatically faulty — the relative clause "by which a witch is riding" is an awkward and incorrect way to describe a picture that shows a witch riding a broomstick.

• Rule: When describing the content of a picture/image, the correct structure is "a picture of + noun/noun phrase", where the noun phrase can itself contain a present participle (riding) describing an ongoing action shown in the picture.

• Applying the rule: "a picture of a witch riding a broomstick" correctly and naturally describes the image.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No improvement" is incorrect because the original phrase "picture by which a witch is riding" is clearly ungrammatical and needs correction.

• Option 2: "picture that of a witch riding" is incorrect because "that of" is redundant and grammatically awkward when directly followed by "a witch riding" — it garbles the sentence structure.

• Option 3: "pictures of witch riding" is incorrect because "witch" is a singular countable noun and requires the article "a" before it ("a witch"); also, the sentence originally refers to a single picture ("There's even a..."), so "pictures" (plural) does not agree with the singular article "a".

NOTE

• The structure "a picture/photo/image of + noun + present participle" is a common construction tested by SSC (e.g., "a photo of a boy playing", "a video of a cat sleeping").

• Always check subject-article agreement: a singular article ("a"/"an") must be followed by a singular noun, never a plural one.

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
The federal government
P. currently provides disaster relief for direct impacts
Q. of volcanic eruptions and other natural disasters,
R. but limited or no assistance for the indirect effects
S. experienced from long periods of volcanic unrest
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. PQRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed opening "The federal government" needs a verb phrase to complete the main clause, which is supplied by P ("currently provides disaster relief for direct impacts").

• Q ("of volcanic eruptions and other natural disasters,") must immediately follow P, since it completes the noun phrase "direct impacts of volcanic eruptions and other natural disasters".

• R ("but limited or no assistance for the indirect effects") introduces the contrasting second half of the sentence using "but", and must follow the first complete clause (P + Q).

• S ("experienced from long periods of volcanic unrest") completes the noun phrase "the indirect effects experienced from long periods of volcanic unrest", so it must directly follow R.

• Correct order: The federal government + P + Q + R + S, i.e. PQRS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (QRPS) is incorrect because it begins with Q, which cannot logically follow "The federal government" without the verb phrase supplied by P first.

• Option 3 (RQPS) is incorrect because it places the contrasting clause R ("but limited or no assistance...") before the main clause P is even introduced, which is illogical since "but" must introduce a contrast to something already stated.

• Option 4 (SPQR) is incorrect because S ("experienced from long periods of volcanic unrest") is placed first, but it grammatically depends on and must follow "the indirect effects", which appears only in R.

NOTE

• In sentence-rearrangement questions with a fixed subject given, always find the segment that supplies the main verb first — that segment must come immediately after the fixed subject.

• Contrast connectors like "but", "however", "yet" always mark the beginning of the second (contrasting) half of a sentence and never come first.

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.
To be ready for a conflict (is one of the most effectual mean of) preserving harmony.
option_2: is one of most effectual means of
option_3: is one of the most effectual means of
option_4: is one of most effectual mean with
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is one of the most effectual means of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The original bracketed phrase contains two errors: the missing article "the" before the superlative "most effectual", and the incorrect singular noun "mean" instead of the correct plural noun "means".

• Rule 1: Superlative adjectives ("most effectual") used to single out one item from a group must be preceded by the definite article "the" — i.e., "one of the most effectual...".

• Rule 2: The noun "means" (a method or way of achieving something) has the same form in both singular and plural, but in the fixed expression "one of the most effectual means of + gerund", the plural form "means" (not "mean") is required.

• Applying both rules: "is one of the most effectual means of preserving harmony" is the grammatically correct form.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No improvement" is incorrect because the original phrase is missing the article "the" and wrongly uses the singular "mean" instead of "means".

• Option 2: "is one of most effectual means of" is incorrect because it is still missing the required article "the" before "most effectual".

• Option 4: "is one of most effectual mean with" is incorrect on three counts: it is missing "the", it wrongly uses the singular "mean", and it incorrectly uses the preposition "with" instead of "of".

NOTE

• "Means" (method/way) does not change form between singular and plural — "a means to an end" (singular) and "several means of transport" (plural) both use "means", never "mean".

• The structure "one of the + superlative adjective + plural noun" always requires the definite article "the" (e.g., "one of the best players", "one of the most difficult questions").

question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, then select the option "No error".
Although people had been on watch and/ the watchkeepers were very tired,/ everyone were up and buzzing.
option_4: Although people had been on watch and
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. everyone were up and buzzing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the subject-verb agreement of the segment "everyone were up and buzzing".

• Rule: The indefinite pronoun "everyone" is always treated as singular and must take a singular verb ("was"), even though it refers to a group of people.

• Correct form: "everyone was up and buzzing."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No error" is incorrect because the sentence does contain a subject-verb agreement error, as explained above.

• Option 2: "the watchkeepers were very tired," is correct as it stands — "watchkeepers" is plural, correctly taking the plural verb "were".

• Option 4: "Although people had been on watch and" is correct — "people" is plural, correctly taking the plural auxiliary "had been", and "Although" correctly introduces the subordinate clause.

NOTE

• Indefinite pronouns that are always singular and take a singular verb: everyone, everybody, everything, someone, somebody, something, anyone, anybody, anything, no one, nobody, nothing, each, either, neither.

• Do not be misled by a plural-sounding meaning — "everyone" refers to people collectively but is grammatically singular.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Blessing in disguise
option_1: A good deed rewards as a blessing
option_2: Bad thing that turns out to be good
option_3: A good thing introduced into your life as a blessing
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bad thing that turns out to be good.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Blessing in disguise" means something that initially seems bad, unfortunate, or unpleasant, but eventually turns out to have a good or beneficial result. (आपत्ति में भी अवसर/जो बुरा लगे पर अंततः अच्छा साबित हो)
◦ Example: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise — it pushed him to start his own business, which became far more successful.

• The word "disguise" means something hidden or masked; the idiom suggests that the true (good) nature of an event is hidden behind its initially bad appearance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "A good deed rewards as a blessing" is incorrect — this describes a straightforward positive outcome of a good action, not the concept of something bad turning good.

• Option 3: "A good thing introduced into your life as a blessing" is incorrect because it describes a plainly good event, with no element of it first appearing bad — the idiom specifically requires an initial negative appearance.

• Option 4: "Something that happens very rarely" is incorrect — this describes rarity/infrequency, which is unrelated to the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• Related idioms with a similar "hidden positive" sense: "Every cloud has a silver lining" (there is something good in every bad situation) and "No pain, no gain" (hardship is necessary for success).

• Do not confuse with "A wolf in sheep's clothing", which means the opposite — something that appears good/harmless but is actually bad/dangerous.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.
Cupidity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Largesse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Cupidity" means an extreme, excessive desire for wealth or possessions; greed. (लालच, धन-लोलुपता)

• The word "Largesse" means generosity in giving money or gifts to others; liberality, which is the direct opposite of greed. (उदारता, दानशीलता)
◦ Example: The old landlord was known throughout the village for his largesse towards the poor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Hatred" (घृणा): an intense feeling of dislike or hostility — this is the opposite of "love", not of "greed".

• Option 3: "Greed" (लालच): an intense desire for wealth or possessions — this is a synonym, not an antonym, of "Cupidity".

• Option 4: "Avarice" (लोभ): extreme greed for wealth — this is also a synonym, not an antonym, of "Cupidity".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Cupidity": Avarice, Greed, Covetousness, Rapacity.

• Other antonyms of "Cupidity"/"Greed": Generosity, Munificence, Liberality, Altruism.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.
The dog chased the ball into the neighbour's yard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The dog chased the ball into the neighbour's yard" narrates a single completed past action, and is already grammatically correct.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense: used for an action that started and finished at a definite point of time in the past. Structure: Subject + V2 (past form) + Object.

• Here, "chased" is the correct past-tense (V2) form of the verb "chase", correctly agreeing with the rest of the sentence, which describes a completed past event.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "chase the ball" is incorrect because the base form (V1) "chase" cannot stand alone as the main verb of a simple past narrative sentence.

• Option 3: "chasing the ball" is incorrect because the present participle "chasing" requires an auxiliary verb (such as "was") to form a complete verb phrase; used alone, it creates a sentence fragment.

• Option 4: "has chasing the ball" is incorrect because the auxiliary "has" must be followed by a past participle (V3), not a present participle — "has chasing" is not a valid verb form.

NOTE

• Do not "correct" a sentence that is already grammatically fine — always check whether the original sentence already follows a valid tense structure before selecting an improvement option.

• The past participle of "chase" is "chased" (regular verb: chase–chased–chased).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.
Add more flour if the dough is too stickiest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. too sticky.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "too stickiest" incorrectly combines the word "too" with the superlative degree ("stickiest") of the adjective.

• Rule: The word "too" (meaning "excessively") is always followed by the positive/base degree of an adjective, never the comparative or superlative degree — e.g., "too hot", "too big", "too sticky" (never "too hottest", "too biggest", "too stickiest").

• Correct form: "too sticky", meaning the dough is excessively sticky.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "too stickier" is incorrect because it combines "too" with the comparative degree ("stickier"), which is equally ungrammatical as combining it with the superlative.

• Option 3: "No improvement" is incorrect because the original phrase "too stickiest" is grammatically wrong, as explained above.

• Option 4: "much stick" is incorrect because it changes the meaning entirely ("stick" is used as a noun/verb here, not the required adjective "sticky"), and does not fit the sentence grammatically.

NOTE

• "Too" vs "so": "too" implies an excessive degree with a negative consequence ("too sticky to handle"), while "so" simply intensifies ("so sticky").

• Degrees of comparison for "sticky": Positive – sticky; Comparative – stickier; Superlative – stickiest. Only the positive form pairs with "too".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom
Pedal to the metal
option_1: To enjoy yourself by going out.
option_2: To go full speed, especially while driving a vehicle.
option_3: Avoid responsibility by giving it to someone else.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To go full speed, especially while driving a vehicle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Pedal to the metal" means to go as fast as possible, especially while driving, i.e., to press the accelerator pedal all the way down to the floor (the metal base) of the vehicle. (पूरी गति से/तेज़ रफ़्तार से)
◦ Example: Once they hit the highway, he put the pedal to the metal and they reached the city in record time.

• The phrase originates from the literal action of a driver pressing the accelerator pedal down as far as it will go, until it touches the metal floor of the car.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "To enjoy yourself by going out" is incorrect — this describes general leisure activity, unrelated to speed or driving.

• Option 3: "Avoid responsibility by giving it to someone else" is incorrect — this describes the idiom "pass the buck", not "pedal to the metal".

• Option 4: "Very excessive" is incorrect — this is too vague and general, and does not capture the specific driving-related sense of speed conveyed by the idiom.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to speed: "At full tilt" (moving as fast as possible), "In a jiffy" (very quickly), "Like greased lightning" (extremely fast).

• Do not confuse with idioms about avoiding responsibility, such as "Pass the buck" or "Wash one's hands of something".

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.
One who helps the needy and the helpless
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Samaritan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Samaritan" (often "Good Samaritan") is one who helps the needy and the helpless, especially a stranger, without expecting anything in return. (परोपकारी व्यक्ति, दूसरों की सहायता करने वाला)
◦ Example: A kind Samaritan stopped to help the stranded motorist change his tyre.

• The term originates from the Biblical parable of the Good Samaritan, who helped an injured traveller when others had ignored him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Novice" (नौसिखिया): a person new to or inexperienced in a field or activity; a beginner.

• Option 2: "Egotist" (आत्मकेंद्रित व्यक्ति): a person who is excessively self-centred or conceited about themselves.

• Option 4: "Highbrow" (उच्च बौद्धिक स्तर का व्यक्ति): a person having, or claiming to have, superior intellectual or cultural tastes.

NOTE

• Other common one-word substitutions related to helping/kindness: Philanthropist (one who promotes the welfare of others, especially through charitable donations), Altruist (one who is unselfishly concerned for the welfare of others), Benefactor (one who gives financial or other help to others).

question:
Choose the option that is the correct passive form of the sentence.
Shivam does not play football.
option_1: Football will not played by Shivam.
option_2: Football is not played by Shivam.
option_3: Football was not played by Shivam.
option_4: Football has not played by Shivam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Football is not played by Shivam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Shivam does not play football" is a negative sentence in the Simple Present Tense.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense (negative):
◦ Active: Subject + does/do not + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + not + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "football" becomes the subject; being singular/uncountable, it takes the auxiliary "is"; the verb "play" becomes the past participle "played"; and "Shivam" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Football is not played by Shivam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will not played" is an invalid verb form — the future auxiliary "will" must be followed by the base form "be played", not "played" alone; moreover, the original sentence is in the present tense, not the future.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "was not played" is the passive form of the Simple Past Tense, not the Simple Present Tense used in the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has not played" is not a valid passive construction (the passive requires "has not been played"), and it also wrongly reflects the Present Perfect Tense rather than the Simple Present Tense.

NOTE

• Passive voice formula chart (negative): Simple Present – is/am/are + not + V3; Simple Past – was/were + not + V3; Present Perfect – has/have + not + been + V3.

• A common trap in SSC passive-voice questions is dropping the auxiliary "be" before the past participle (e.g., writing "will played" instead of "will be played").

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.
Contempt
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Approbation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Contempt" means the feeling that a person or a thing is beneath consideration, worthless, or deserving scorn; disdain. (तिरस्कार, अवमानना)

• The word "Approbation" means approval, praise, or official sanction of something, which is the direct opposite of contempt/scorn. (अनुमोदन, प्रशंसा)
◦ Example: The young officer's brave conduct earned the approbation of his seniors.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Opprobrium" (कलंक, अपमान): harsh criticism or scornful reproach resulting from disgraceful behaviour — a synonym, not antonym, of contempt.

• Option 3: "Odium" (घृणा): widespread hatred or strong disgust directed at a person because of something they have done — also a synonym of contempt.

• Option 4: "Obloquy" (निंदा): strong public criticism or verbal abuse; disgrace — again a synonym, not antonym, of contempt.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Contempt": Scorn, Disdain, Derision, Disparagement.

• Other antonyms of "Contempt": Admiration, Respect, Esteem, Regard.

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Artefect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Artefact" (British English) or "Artifact" (American English) — an object made by a human being, typically one of historical or cultural interest. (कलाकृति, ऐतिहासिक वस्तु)
◦ Example: Archaeologists discovered several ancient artefacts at the excavation site.

• Spelling key: the word is built from "arte-" (art/skill) + "fact" (made) — the ending is "-fact", not "-fect". The word printed as "Artefect" wrongly replaces the "a" in "-fact" with an "e".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Articulate" is correctly spelled — meaning able to express oneself clearly, or to pronounce clearly.

• Option 2: "Arduous" is correctly spelled — meaning involving strenuous effort; difficult and tiring.

• Option 3: "Arrogate" is correctly spelled — meaning to claim or take something without justification.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the ending "-fact" (as in artefact, factual) with "-fect" (as in defect, perfect, effect) — both endings exist in English, but each word has only one correct form.

• Other commonly confused/misspelt SSC words: bureaucracy, questionnaire, embarrass, occurrence, liaison, harass.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3: "Devilry" (शैतानी, जादू-टोना): wicked or malicious behaviour, or the practice of black magic — again a synonym, not antonym.

• Option 4: "Dismiss" (खारिज करना): to send away or reject something/someone — this is a verb unrelated in meaning to "sorcery" and does not function as its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Sorcery": Witchcraft, Magic, Necromancy, Enchantment.

• Other antonyms of "Sorcery": Science, Fact, Truth.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, after which they were 1.________ by World War II. The Olympics 2.________ in 1948 and was 3.________ held every four years. Until 1992, the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 4.________ by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on 5.________ four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No.1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. interrupted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states that the Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, and then World War II caused a break in this regular pattern.

• The verb "interrupted" means to stop something temporarily before it is finished, or to break the continuity of a process, which correctly conveys that the regular four-year cycle of the Games was broken/paused by the war.

• Contextual fit: "...after which they were interrupted by World War II" — this logically explains why no Games were held between 1936 and 1948.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "complicated" is incorrect because it means "made more difficult or complex", which does not fit the context of the Games simply being stopped/paused by the war.

• Option 3: "corrupted" is incorrect because it means "made dishonest or of lower moral standard", which is unrelated to the scheduling of the Olympic Games.

• Option 4: "solicited" is incorrect because it means "asked for or requested", which does not make sense in the context of the Games being affected by a war.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the surrounding sentence(s) fully before choosing an option — the correct word must fit both the grammar and the logical meaning of the entire context, not just sound plausible in isolation.

• Words related to "interrupted": suspended, paused, halted, discontinued — all of which fit the idea of a temporary stoppage.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, after which they were 1.________ by World War II. The Olympics 2.________ in 1948 and was 3.________ held every four years. Until 1992, the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 4.________ by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on 5.________ four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No.2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. resumed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Since the passage has just stated that the Games were interrupted by World War II, the natural continuation is that the Olympics started again/resumed once the war ended.

• The verb "resumed" means to begin again after a pause or interruption, which correctly conveys that the Olympic Games restarted in 1948 after being interrupted since 1936.

• Contextual fit: "The Olympics resumed in 1948..." — logically follows from the earlier mention of the Games being interrupted by the war.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "accustomed" is incorrect because it means "used to something through familiarity", which does not fit the idea of the Games starting again after a break.

• Option 3: "confirmed" is incorrect because it means "established the truth of something", which is unrelated to the idea of the Games restarting.

• Option 4: "transformed" is incorrect because it means "changed completely in form or appearance", which is not what happened — the Olympics simply started again in their original four-year pattern, without any such transformation being described.

NOTE

• "Resume" and "interrupt" are commonly paired opposite-action words in cloze passages — after an interruption is mentioned, look for the word that logically signals a restart.

• Related words: recommence, restart, continue (after a pause).

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, after which they were 1.________ by World War II. The Olympics 2.________ in 1948 and was 3.________ held every four years. Until 1992, the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 4.________ by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on 5.________ four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No.3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. again.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes the Olympics resuming in 1948 and then continuing to be held every four years, just as they had been before the war interrupted them.

• The adverb "again" means once more, as before, correctly conveying that the four-yearly pattern of holding the Games returned to what it had been prior to the interruption.

• Contextual fit: "...and was again held every four years" — this correctly links back to the earlier statement that "The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936", showing the pattern resumed unchanged.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "regain" is incorrect because it is a verb ("to get something back"), whereas the blank grammatically requires an adverb modifying "held" — "regain" cannot grammatically follow "was" in this construction.

• Option 2: "bargained" is incorrect because it means "negotiated over terms", which is meaningless in the context of how often the Games were held.

• Option 4: "never" is incorrect because it directly contradicts the passage, which goes on to state that the Games continued to be held every four years until 1992.

NOTE

• Pay attention to part of speech required by the blank — here "was ___ held" needs an adverb, which immediately rules out verbs like "regain" or "bargained".

• "Again" is frequently used in cloze passages to signal the resumption or repetition of a previously established pattern.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, after which they were 1.________ by World War II. The Olympics 2.________ in 1948 and was 3.________ held every four years. Until 1992, the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 4.________ by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on 5.________ four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No.4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. decision.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a formal ruling made "by the International Olympic Committee (IOC)" in 1986 to change the scheduling of the Summer and Winter Games.

• The noun "decision" means a conclusion or resolution reached after consideration, especially one made by an authoritative body, which correctly describes a formal ruling made by the IOC.

• Contextual fit: "...but in accordance with a 1986 decision by the International Olympic Committee (IOC)..." — this correctly conveys that the IOC officially resolved to separate the Summer and Winter Games cycles.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "precision" is incorrect because it means "exactness or accuracy", which does not describe an act of ruling or resolving made by a committee.

• Option 2: "incision" is incorrect because it means "a surgical cut", which is completely unrelated to the context of a committee's ruling.

• Option 4: "indecision" is incorrect because it means "the inability to make a decision", which is the opposite of what is described — the IOC did in fact take definite action to alter the scheduling.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-cision" are often confused in SSC vocabulary questions: decision (a conclusion reached), precision (exactness), incision (a cut), indecision (inability to decide) — each has a distinct, unrelated meaning despite the similar spelling.

• "In accordance with a decision by [authority]" is a common formal collocation used to describe official rulings.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.

The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, after which they were 1.________ by World War II. The Olympics 2.________ in 1948 and was 3.________ held every four years. Until 1992, the Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years, but in accordance with a 1986 4.________ by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on 5.________ four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No.5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. separate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage explains that until 1992 the Winter and Summer Games were held in the same years, but the 1986 IOC decision changed this arrangement so that, from 1994 onward, the Winter Olympics fell in different (even-numbered) years from the Summer Olympics.

• The adjective "separate" means existing or considered individually, apart from something else, which correctly conveys that the Summer and Winter Games were placed on two distinct, non-overlapping four-year cycles rather than sharing the same year.

• Contextual fit: "...to place the Summer and Winter Games on separate four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994" — this matches the fact that the Winter Games (1994) no longer coincided with the Summer Games' cycle (1996), confirming the two events were now on separate schedules.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "customary" is incorrect because it means "usual or traditional", which contradicts the passage's description of a new, changed arrangement introduced in 1986.

• Option 2: "matching" is incorrect because it means "corresponding to/being the same as", which is the opposite of the new arrangement — the whole point of the 1986 decision was to make the two cycles different, not matching.

• Option 3: "together" is incorrect because it implies the Games remained combined/simultaneous, which again contradicts the passage's description of the new alternating, staggered schedule.

NOTE

• This passage is based on real Olympic history: since 1994, the Winter Olympics have been held in the even years exactly between Summer Olympics (e.g., Summer 1996, Winter 1998, Summer 2000, Winter 2002...), so that the two events no longer fall in the same year.

• In cloze passages, options that mean the opposite of the required word (e.g., "matching"/"together" vs. "separate") are common distractors — always check the logical direction of the sentence (continuation vs. contrast) before selecting.
